title: Compatibility of the affine Picard quotient with field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], and let $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ be a smooth proper connected compactification [lem-sc-compactification] with finite boundary $S=\overline C\setminus C$ and $P_0\in S$. Then: (1) $\overline C_{k'}$ is a smooth proper connected compactification of $C_{k'}$ with boundary $S_{k'}=\{P_{k'}:P\in S\}$ (each $P\in S$ pulls back to a single $k'$-point $P_{k'}$), and $\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P)$ pulls back to $\mathcal O_{\overline C_{k'}}(P_{k'})$. (2) Restriction of invertible modules $\mathcal L\mapsto\mathcal L|_C$ defines a surjective homomorphism $J_{\overline C}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ with kernel $\Lambda=\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle$ (identifications of [def-sc-jacobian], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]); this induced isomorphism $J_{\overline C}(k)/\Lambda\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is an isomorphism as in [lem-sc-pic-affine], and likewise $J_{\overline C_{k'}}(k')/\Lambda'\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C_{k'})$ with $\Lambda'=\langle[P_{k'}]-[P_{0,k'}]:P\in S\rangle$. (3) Pullback $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C_{k'})$ corresponds, under these identifications, to the Jacobian base-change map $J_{\overline C}(k)\to J_{\overline C_{k'}}(k')$ of [lem-sc-genus-invariant]; it maps $\Lambda$ isomorphically onto $\Lambda'$, and the isomorphisms of (2) identify pullback $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C_{k'})$ with the induced map $J_{\overline C}(k)/\Lambda\to J_{\overline C_{k'}}(k')/\Lambda'$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-base-change-curve] the base change $\overline C_{k'}$ is a smooth proper curve over $k'$ and $C_{k'}$ is a smooth affine curve, and the open immersion base changes to the open immersion $C_{k'}\hookrightarrow\overline C_{k'}$. Connectedness: $k$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed, so the connected $k$-schemes $\overline C$ and $C$ are geometrically connected by [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected]; by the definition of geometric connectedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] their base changes $\overline C_{k'}$ and $C_{k'}$ are connected. Boundary: $S$ is a finite set of closed points of $\overline C$, which is of finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$, so each $P\in S$ has $\kappa(P)=k$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], i.e. $P$ is the image of a closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\overline C$. Its base change is a closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\overline C_{k'}$, a single $k'$-point $P_{k'}$. The complement $\overline C_{k'}\setminus C_{k'}$ is the preimage of $S$ under $\overline C_{k'}\to\overline C$, i.e. the union of the fibres $P\times_kk'=\{P_{k'}\}$, so $S_{k'}=\{P_{k'}:P\in S\}$ is finite and $\overline C_{k'}$ is a smooth proper connected compactification of $C_{k'}$ in the sense of [lem-sc-compactification]. Since $\overline C_{k'}\to\overline C$ is flat (base change of the flat morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$) and the effective Cartier divisor $P$ pulls back to $P\times_{\overline C}\overline C_{k'}=P_{k'}$, [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-properties] (2) gives $\mathcal O_{\overline C_{k'}}(P_{k'})\cong(\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P))_{k'}$.

source.place: Affine case, compactification and boundary paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-pic-restriction-boundary] to the compactification over $k$ and, after base change, to the compactification over $k'$. Under the Jacobian compatibility clause of [lem-sc-genus-invariant], the pullback on $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ is the Jacobian base-change map. Restriction is therefore surjective in both cases, and its kernel is respectively generated by the boundary classes; the resulting quotient isomorphisms are the isomorphisms of [lem-sc-pic-affine].

By step 1 and [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-properties] (2), pullback sends $[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P)]-[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P_0)]$ to $[\mathcal O_{\overline C_{k'}}(P_{k'})]-[\mathcal O_{\overline C_{k'}}(P_{0,k'})]$, so by step 2 the Jacobian base-change map sends each generator $[P]-[P_0]$ of $\Lambda$ to the generator $[P_{k'}]-[P_{0,k'}]$ of $\Lambda'$; hence it maps $\Lambda$ onto $\Lambda'$. It is injective on all of $J_{\overline C}(k)$: via $J_{\overline C_{k'}}\cong(J_{\overline C})_{k'}$ of [lem-sc-genus-invariant] it is the map $J_{\overline C}(k)\to J_{\overline C}(k')$ given by composing with $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is injective for any $k$-scheme (a $k$-point $x$ is determined by its image point and the $k$-isomorphism $\kappa(x)\to k$, and both are recovered from the composite since $k\to k'$ is injective). So $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ is an isomorphism and the map descends to $J_{\overline C}(k)/\Lambda\to J_{\overline C_{k'}}(k')/\Lambda'$. Finally pullback commutes with restriction to the open subscheme, $(\mathcal L_{k'})|_{C_{k'}}=(\mathcal L|_C)_{k'}$ (the square of $C_{k'}\hookrightarrow\overline C_{k'}$ over $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ commutes), so the restriction maps of [lem-sc-pic-restriction-boundary] over $k$ and $k'$ intertwine pullback on $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ with pullback $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C_{k'})$, which is the asserted identification.
